outline.chapter_title: From Text Prompts to Controlled Images: Motivation and Overview
outline.description: Introduce the need for controllability in text-to-image diffusion models and position Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) as a principled, efficient finetuning paradigm that preserves pretrained semantics while enabling downstream control.
subtopics: Limitations of pure text guidance for fine-grained control
Two target tasks: subject-driven generation and controllable generation
Finetuning desiderata: efficiency and preservation of generalization
Key idea: preserve neuron angular relations via orthogonal transforms
Contributions of OFT and COFT and high-level empirical gains

outline.chapter_title: Background: Diffusion Models, Conditioning, and Finetuning Strategies
outline.description: Provide essential background on latent diffusion models, common conditioning mechanisms, and standard finetuning or adapter-based approaches used for personalization and controllability.
subtopics: Denoising diffusion and latent diffusion basics
Stable Diffusion architecture: UNet and cross-attention conditioning
Subject-driven generation (e.g., DreamBooth) and its challenges
Controllable generation (e.g., ControlNet, T2I-Adapter) and overhead
Standard finetuning, adapter modules, and LoRA: strengths and limits

outline.chapter_title: Mathematical Foundations: Angles, Hyperspheres, and Orthogonal Transforms
outline.description: Develop the geometric intuition that neuron directions (angles) encode semantics, formalize hyperspherical energy, and explain why orthogonal transformations preserve this structure.
subtopics: Cosine similarity and neuron direction versus magnitude
Hyperspherical energy: definition and what it measures
Invariance of pairwise angles under a shared orthogonal transform
Why angular information captures semantics (Fourier phase analogy)
Toy evidence: angle-only activations reconstruct semantics better than magnitude

outline.description: Present OFT as learning a layer-shared orthogonal matrix that rotates pretrained neurons to adapt to a downstream task while exactly preserving hyperspherical energy.
subtopics: Objective: minimize change in hyperspherical energy between pretrained and finetuned layers
Forward pass transformation: W' = R · W0 with R orthogonal
Identity initialization for zero-start finetuning
View as adjusting the neuron coordinate system while preserving pairwise angles
Equivalence to a structured weight update: ΔW = (R − I) · W0
Where to apply OFT in diffusion models (e.g., attention weights)

outline.description: Detail practical parameterizations of orthogonal matrices for large models, emphasizing computational efficiency and parameter efficiency compared to LoRA.
subtopics: Why naive orthogonalization (e.g., Gram–Schmidt) is too costly
Cayley transform: R = (I + Q)(I − Q)^{-1} with skew-symmetric Q
Consequences of special orthogonal group (determinant +1) and practical impact
Block-diagonal R with r blocks: parameter and compute savings
Optional block sharing across channels or heads
Parameter complexity versus LoRA and concrete 128×128 example

outline.description: Introduce COFT, which augments OFT with a radius constraint around the pretrained weights to further stabilize finetuning and control deviation.
subtopics: Adding a constraint on deviation from identity: ||R − I|| ≤ ε
Relating the constraint to Cayley parameters via Neumann series
Projected gradient descent on Q to enforce ||Q|| ≤ ε′
Effect of ε: flexibility–stability trade-off and practical tuning
Initialization and stability benefits observed empirically

outline.description: Extend OFT by learning per-neuron magnitudes in addition to angles, which preserves hyperspherical energy while granting extra flexibility.
subtopics: Adding a positive diagonal scaling D on neuron outputs
Why scaling does not affect hyperspherical energy
Forward pass with both R and D, and parameter overhead
When re-scaled OFT helps and interplay with COFT
Implementation note and errata clarification

outline.description: Explain how OFT integrates into the DreamBooth framework to preserve subject identity with few images while improving training stability and convergence.
subtopics: DreamBooth setup: reconstruction and class-preserving losses
Finetuning targets (e.g., attention layers) with OFT/COFT
Stability across iterations versus catastrophic collapse
Metrics: DINO and CLIP-I for subject fidelity, CLIP-T for prompt fidelity, LPIPS for diversity
Empirical patterns: faster convergence, stronger identity preservation, and prompt adherence

outline.description: Demonstrate OFT for conditioning on external signals such as edges, segmentation, and landmarks, achieving accurate control without extra inference overhead.
subtopics: Control signals: Canny edges (C2I), segmentation maps (S2I), facial landmarks (L2F)
Datasets and setups: COCO, ADE20K, CelebA-HQ
Design contrast: OFT versus ControlNet/T2I-Adapter (no extra inference cost)
Control consistency metrics: IoU/F1 for edges, mIoU/accuracy for segmentation, landmark L2
Observed benefits: faster, smoother convergence and stronger control

outline.description: Summarize quantitative and qualitative findings across tasks and dissect the effects of key hyperparameters and design choices.
subtopics: Convergence speed and stability: OFT/COFT vs DreamBooth, LoRA, ControlNet, T2I-Adapter
Final performance on subject fidelity, prompt fidelity, diversity
Control quality across C2I, S2I, L2F with new consistency metrics
Data and parameter efficiency, including small-data regimes
Ablations: number of blocks r, block sharing, ε in COFT, re-scaled OFT
Preliminary results on convolutional layers and qualitative examples
No additional inference overhead via weight folding

outline.description: Deepen understanding of why OFT works, relate it to existing techniques, and articulate the flexibility–regularity trade-off in finetuning.
subtopics: Why angles encode semantics and the manifold view of optimization
Why minimizing hyperspherical energy is unsuitable for finetuning
Relationship to LoRA: low-rank additive vs full-rank orthogonal multiplicative updates
Two routes to parameter efficiency: rank versus structured sparsity
Architecture agnosticism and potential for convolutional and transformer layers
Compositionality of orthogonal transforms across tasks

outline.description: Provide a practical recipe for implementing OFT/COFT in modern diffusion pipelines, including tuning, debugging, and deployment.
subtopics: Layer selection (e.g., attention q/k/v/proj) and sharing strategies
Cayley-parameterized orthogonal module: initialization and stability
Choosing r, block sharing, and ε (for COFT)
Optimizers, learning rates, and training schedules
Projected updates for COFT and maintaining invertibility of (I − Q)
Monitoring orthogonality and hyperspherical energy preservation
Folding R into W0 for zero-overhead inference
Common pitfalls and debugging tips

outline.description: Discuss open problems and broader impacts, including computational bottlenecks, multi-task composition, and responsible deployment.
subtopics: Scalability of Cayley inverse and alternatives (matrix exponential, Householder, Givens)
Improving parameter efficiency without strong structural bias
Compositional finetuning and interference across tasks
Beyond hyperspherical energy: richer measures of semantic preservation
Ethical considerations in personalization and controllable synthesis
Reproducibility and benchmarking recommendations

outline.description: Hands-on activities to internalize concepts, implement OFT/COFT, and reproduce key empirical findings.
subtopics: Implement an OFT layer with Cayley parameterization and block-diagonal structure
Replicate the angle-versus-magnitude toy experiment
Finetune a small diffusion UNet with OFT vs LoRA and compare convergence
Ablate r and ε and measure hyperspherical energy preservation
Implement and apply control consistency metrics on C2I, S2I, L2F
Compose multiple OFT transforms and study interference
Extend OFT to convolutional layers (depth-wise vs shared blocks)
